## Plan

**Files that differ between the current version and the target version**

- `/workspace/src/click/core.py` vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/src/click/core.py`
- `/workspace/tests/test_arguments.py` vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/tests/test_arguments.py`
- `/workspace/CHANGES.md` vs `/megabit/.megabit_ref/CHANGES.md`

### What is wrong for the user today

In the current code, an argument's help row helper (the function that gives an argument's name and description for the help page) returns nothing at all when the argument has no help text. I confirmed this in `/workspace/src/click/core.py`, in `Argument.get_help_record`, which is declared as able to return `None` and does exactly that when `self.help` is `None`.

Because of that, the help page code in the same file (`Command.format_arguments`) has to build a fallback row itself: it asks each argument for its help row and, if the answer is nothing, makes a row out of the argument's name plus an empty description. The help page already lists every positional argument once at least one of them is documented, so the fallback only duplicates what `get_help_record` should be returning on its own.

The missing row is a problem for anyone who writes their own help output or asks an argument directly for its name and description — for example a custom help page, a tool that lists a command's arguments, or a wrapper that formats them. They get nothing back and have to work out the metavar and the empty description themselves.

### What the target version does

In the reference directory, `Argument.get_help_record` is declared to always return a pair: the argument's name and its help text, with an empty description when there is no help text. It also gained a docstring explaining that it never returns nothing, and a version note. The help page code in `format_arguments` then just collects those pairs directly, with the manual fallback removed.

The reference version of `/megabit/.megabit_ref/CHANGES.md` adds a note about this: the argument help record always returns a pair, and used to return nothing for an argument with no help.

The reference version of `/megabit/.megabit_ref/tests/test_arguments.py` adds a test named `test_argument_get_help_record_never_none`, which checks the three cases: no help text gives the name plus an empty description, an empty help string gives the same, and a documented argument gives its name and its help text.

### Files in the current workspace that are about the problem (Hints candidates)

- `/workspace/src/click/core.py` — contains `Argument.get_help_record` (around line 3806) and `Command.format_arguments` (around line 1312)
- `/workspace/tests/test_arguments.py` — where the help-output tests for arguments live
- `/workspace/CHANGES.md` — where the note about the positional arguments help section already sits
- `/workspace/src/click/core.py` also holds `Option.get_help_record` (around line 3401), which is the sibling behavior for options that the new docstring points at

### Impact

Usability and correctness for anything that reads an argument's help row. The help page text stays the same as it is now, since the fallback was already producing the same rows; what changes is that asking an argument directly now always gives an answer.

{"content":"# Asking an argument for its help line gives nothing back when it has no help text

## What happens now

When you ask a command line argument for the line that shows up in the help page, and that argument has no help text written for it, you get nothing back at all. Nothing is returned, so there is no name and no description to show. The built-in help page still lists the argument, but only because it builds that line itself as a fallback. Anything else you write that asks an argument for its help line has to build the name and the empty description on its own.

## What should happen

Asking an argument for its help line should always give something back: the argument's name, plus its help text, or an empty description when the argument has no help text. You should never have to check for a missing answer first.

## About this project

Click is a Python library for building command line programs. You describe your commands, options and arguments in Python, and Click turns them into a working command line program, including the help page users read with the help option.

## Problem this solves

If you build your own help output, a listing of a command's arguments, or a wrapper that formats them, an argument with no help text gives you nothing, and your code has to special-case it. That is the one case you should not have to worry about, and it makes every caller longer than it needs to be.

## What changed

Arguments now always hand back their name and their description, with an empty description when there is no help text. The extra fallback line that the built-in help page built on its own is gone, so the help page still reads the same but now gets every argument's line from one place. The entry about this was added to the project's list of changes.

## Impact

Ease of use and correctness for anything that reads an argument's help line.

## User experience

Before: you write a small script that prints each argument of a command with its description. One argument has no help text, so it prints an empty line, or you add your own special handling for that one case.

After: you print each argument with its description the same way for all of them, and the argument with no help text simply shows its name with an empty description.
